name: Logic

papers.title: Separable models of an NIP Banach space theory
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be the renorming of $\ell_2(\mathbb N)\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb N)$ with norm $(h^2+q^2)^{1/2}$, where $h$ is the Hilbert norm and $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. We prove that the unstable theory $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$ is NIP in the pure Banach language. We recover the index order from the Banach norm and classify the continuum many separable models up to surjective linear isometry. The invariants are the order type of a countable model of $\operatorname{Th}(\mathbb N,<)$ and the dimension of a separable Hilbert summand. Every such pair occurs. We describe all elementary embeddings between these models. The bounded norm types over a separable model are separable in the uniform metric exactly when its index order contains no copy of $(\mathbb Q,<)$.

papers.title: A Sequent Calculus for the Quantified Reflection Calculus $\mathrm{QRC}_1$: Cut-Elimination, Interpolation, and NP-Completeness
papers.abstract: We introduce $\mathrm{G3QRC}_1$, the first Gentzen-style sequent calculus for Borges and Joosten's Quantified Reflection Calculus ($\mathrm{QRC}_1$). As a strictly positive, first-order modal logic, $\mathrm{QRC}_1$ crucially escapes Vardanyan's $\Pi^0_2$-completeness theorem for quantified provability logic, while remaining arithmetically complete with respect to Peano and Heyting Arithmetic. The central innovation of $\mathrm{G3QRC}_1$ is a pair of context-erasing modal rules that simultaneously account for the monotonicity and transitivity axioms by deliberately discarding parametric context across modal boundaries. This structural bottleneck allows for a clean proof of cut-admissibility via a standard lexicographic induction, circumventing the complex loop-checking typically required for provability logics. Cut admissibility yields an instantiated subformula property and supports a direct canonical proof of the finite model property. We streamline the adequate Kripke semantics by interpreting constants globally. We also establish a split-context Craig interpolation theorem and a contextual form of left uniform interpolation, uniformly eliminating private predicate symbols, constants, and free parameters. Finally, by leveraging the rigid structural constraints of the context-erasing rules and the absence of left-branching connectives, we prove that, over the standard fixed countable signatures specified in the paper, the decision problem for $\mathrm{QRC}_1$ is $\mathbf{NP}$-complete, situating this quantified modal logic in a comparatively low nondeterministic complexity class.

papers.title: Stability in abstract classes via set theoretic techniques
papers.abstract: We prove that all abstract classes equipped with an independence relation satisfying a mild local character condition are stable. We obtain the result by using methods from model theory and set theory. We have several applications in the context of abstract classes of modules. In particular, we prove that if $K$ is a class of $R$-modules closed under isomorphisms and pure submodules and $\lambda^{\operatorname{card}(R) + \aleph_0} = \lambda$, then $K$ equipped with pure embeddings is stable in $\lambda$.

papers.title: A family of forcings with hyperfinite equivalence of generics
papers.abstract: We identify a class of forcings that includes several classical forcings and prove that for all forcings $\mathbb{P}$ in this class the associated equivalence of generics relation $\equiv^{\mathbb{P}}_M$, as defined by Smythe, is a hyperfinite CBER.

papers.title: Well-foundedness of the strict Lipschitz order on countably complete filters
papers.abstract: In $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{DC}$, the strict Lipschitz order on proper countably complete filters on any fixed ordinal is well-founded. The proof uses transfinite recursion and closure under countable intersections to derive a contradiction from a descending chain. Restricting each filter to the least ordinal it contains yields a set-like well-founded order that compares filters on different ordinals. In $\mathsf{ZF}$, two ultrafilters on the same ordinal are equal if each is nonexpansively reducible to the other. These results answer both parts of Question 9.2.11 in The Ultrapower Axiom.

papers.title: Higher-Dimensional Automata in Geometric Logic
papers.abstract: What does the topos of a higher-dimensional automaton know about its infinite behaviour that its language does not? We write partial HDAs with an infinite run as models of a geometric theory over an intuitionistic metatheory with no choice. The topos of a machine is that of sheaves on its prefixes. The label word of a prefix records the shape and acceptance bit of each cell with the ipomset of each step. Under unique choice these words give a geometric morphism to the label topos of sheaves on label words, which thus records the shapes and acceptance bits that the B\"uchi language forgets. Machines sharing their B\"uchi language and their frames can differ over the label topos. The bouquet of two squares shares its frame and its B\"uchi language with the interleaved square; each accepted run of either reads the two events in parallel forever. Only the interleaved square has runs through cells of shape a, and the geometric sequent excluding such runs separates the two over the label topos. Over alphabets with decidable equality, finite rigid machines are unambiguous exactly when their label maps are inclusions of locales, and their equivalence over the label topos is decided whenever either is unambiguous. Equivalences of frames over the label topos transport points with their labels, and the invariants of fibres and of the language of points follow from this transport. On finite partial HDAs over alphabets with decidable equality, Muller and B\"uchi acceptance coincide exactly under a weak form of excluded middle.
